statement: Move selected elements by dragging with graphical or Tracker-typed distance, optionally leaving the original in place for one copy or repeating the placement for several copies, with 3D drags constrained to the editing plane.

source.ref: Dragging Elements (drag, drag a copy, drag multiple copies)

superiority: Numeric and graphic input share one undoable operation with live dimension preview.

acceptance.sketch: Move wall by (2,3,0) numerically: end points shift exactly, attached doors travel with it.

notes: CORRECTED — read Dragging Elements; Drag, Drag a Copy and Drag Multiple Copies exist, 3D drag is limited to the editing plane. Elevation change is a separate Elevate command (see EDIT-0004); no separate two-point vector command found.

statement: Rotate selected elements about a clicked centre by a graphically defined or Tracker-typed angle, with an optional rotated copy and a quick 90-degree step in either direction.
superiority: Works equally for groups, curved walls and library objects without drift.

acceptance.sketch: Rotate 90 degrees about origin: vertices map to (x,y)->(-y,x) within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Rotating Elements; centre click, start point and end point (or typed angle) define the rotation; rotate-a-copy and quick 90-degree clockwise/counterclockwise commands exist.

statement: Mirror selected elements about an axis given by two clicks, optionally as a copy, with doors and windows remaining in line with their host wall.
superiority: Handedness fixes apply to composites and profile skins with an explicit report.

acceptance.sketch: Mirror door about vertical axis: swing flips and the reveal side stays correct.

notes: CORRECTED — read Mirroring Elements; axis is two clicks, Ctrl gives a mirrored copy, doors/windows stay in their wall; text and dimensions are not flipped, only their box. Stair handedness is not mentioned.

statement: Raise or lower selected elements along Z by a typed amount, with an option to reassign each element's home story from its new elevation.
superiority: Elevation edits preview as a section ghost.

acceptance.sketch: Elevate slab by 0.5: all vertices z += 0.5 within 1e-12.

notes: CORRECTED — read Elevating Elements; the Elevate dialog takes a delta value plus a Set Home Story by Elevation checkbox. It is a relative shift, not a choice of reference level.

statement: Create any number of copies of selected elements along a path using a Multiply action (drag, rotate, elevate or rectangular matrix) and one of four input methods that fix the count, the spacing or both.
superiority: Array stays editable as a pattern object until baked.

acceptance.sketch: 5 copies at 2 m spacing yields six elements positioned at 2k within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Multiply Elements; actions are Drag, Rotate, Elevate and Matrix; input methods are Increment and Spread, Increment, Spread and Distribute; copies can follow a picked path, be rotated or randomised, and carry a vertical displacement.

statement: Enlarge or reduce selected elements by a ratio typed numerically or drawn graphically about a chosen fixed point, with options to scale wall and column thickness, library parts, text and markers.
superiority: Non-uniform scaling refuses elements that lose validity and explains why.

acceptance.sketch: Scale 2x about origin doubles distances; volume x8.

notes: CORRECTED — read Resize (Enlarge or Reduce) Elements; a single ratio is entered so scaling is uniform, non-uniform scaling is not documented; grouped elements are unaffected unless the group is suspended.

statement: Stretch linear and polygonal elements along a two-point vector so that only nodes inside a marquee move, while elements wholly inside it are dragged intact and locked elements stay fixed.
superiority: Stretch keeps constraints and associated openings.

acceptance.sketch: Stretch marquee moving one edge of slab by 1: area changes by edge length.

notes: VERIFIED — read Stretching with the Marquee Tool; also available as Edit > Reshape > Stretch; not available in the 3D window; columns and objects are dragged rather than stretched.

statement: Distribute selected elements evenly along X, Y or a diagonal between the two outermost ones, anchored on bounding boxes or on a user-chosen point through a Special Distribute option.
superiority: Distribute includes parametric elements with live preview.

acceptance.sketch: 5 columns distributed between 0 and 8: gaps 2 within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Distribute Elements and Special Distribute; modes are Along X, Along Y, Along XY and Special; a gap-based mode is not documented (Multiply has a separate Distribute input method).

statement: Align selected elements to the left, right, top, bottom or a centre line of their bounding boxes, or through Special Align to a chosen anchor point on a drawn or existing line, arc or edge.
superiority: Align respects anchored elements and reports conflicts.

acceptance.sketch: Align 4 objects left to reference: min x equal within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Align Elements; commands need at least two selected elements; Special Align lets you pick the anchor point and align to a temporary line/arc or an existing edge.

statement: Split selected walls, beams, slabs, roofs, meshes, fills, zones and linear 2D elements along a drawn line, arc or existing edge, keeping the clicked side selected.
superiority: Split retains properties and attached windows.

acceptance.sketch: Split wall at midpoint yields two walls whose lengths sum to the original.

notes: VERIFIED — read Splitting Elements; splits at every intersection, splitting plane is vertical, Morphs can split along the editing plane; roofs cannot be split by an arc.

statement: Adjust the endpoints of walls, beams, railings, arcs and lines to extend or shorten them to a drawn or clicked line, arc or edge, and trim segments between intersections with a scissors command.
superiority: Join semantic preserved when members subsequently change.

acceptance.sketch: Adjust two walls to intersect: reference lines meet at corner.

notes: CORRECTED — read Adjusting Elements and Trim Elements Using Scissors; Adjust targets a line/arc/edge, not an arbitrary point; Trim removes the clicked part between nearest intersections; roof/shell trim is a separate feature (see SEO-0013).

statement: Round (fillet) or cut (chamfer) the junction of two lines, polylines or walls, or the corners of a polygon, by a given radius, applied to one node or to all corners.
superiority: Same command works on polylines, slabs and walls.

acceptance.sketch: Fillet radius 0.5 between two perpendicular lines: arc tangent to both within 1e-9.

notes: VERIFIED — read Create a Fillet or Chamfer; radius is auto-limited when it would pass a neighbouring vertex; commands do not act on grouped elements unless groups are suspended.

statement: Offset all edges of a polygonal element, spline or chain of connected elements by dragging, optionally leaving the original and placing one or several offset copies.
superiority: Offset copies carry through to curved elements exactly.

acceptance.sketch: Offset 0.5 of square: side length changes by 1.0 on a corner-closed chain.

notes: CORRECTED — read Offset All Edges; works on polygonal elements, splines and selected connected elements of one type; Ctrl makes a copy and Ctrl+Alt several; a ghost contour previews the result.

statement: Intersect two selected lines, polylines, arcs, walls or beams so they meet at the nearest of their endpoints, provided both are visible on the same story.
superiority: Intersect resolves ties by deterministic rule.

acceptance.sketch: After Intersect, both reference lines end at the intersection to 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Intersect Two Elements; the command joins ends at their nearest meeting point and may need repeating for the second end of lines; it is not a fillet.

statement: Group selected elements so they move, rotate, mirror, multiply and delete together, with nested groups, a Suspend Groups toggle to edit single members, and an Autogroup mode.
superiority: Groups are named containers with metadata and selective suspend.

acceptance.sketch: Group of 3 elements moves as one; Suspend Groups allows edit of one.

notes: CORRECTED — read Group Elements; Group, Ungroup, Suspend Groups and Autogroup exist; dimensions, zones and labels cannot be grouped; fillet and unify need the group suspended.

statement: Lock selected elements, or whole layers, against accidental edits while leaving them selectable and usable for snapping and parameter pickup, with an Unlock All command.
superiority: Per-property lock with permission model in cloud.

acceptance.sketch: Locked wall refuses move; snap to its corner works.

notes: VERIFIED — read Lock/Unlock Elements; locked elements remain usable for relative construction, Snap Guides and parameter transfer.

statement: Control on which stories a construction element is displayed and editable by choosing between its home story only and all stories it physically intersects.
superiority: Multi-storey visibility rule is first-class (see A30).

acceptance.sketch: Wall shown on story +1 displays cut at plan.

notes: CORRECTED — read Show On Stories; options for walls, slabs, roofs, shells, morphs, meshes, beams and columns are Home Story Only and All Relevant Stories (this page lists no above/below variants).

statement: Reshape polygonal and chained elements through pet palette commands such as moving a node, offsetting an edge, inserting a node and curving an edge.
superiority: Edit nodes by typing exact coordinates.

acceptance.sketch: Insert node on slab edge keeps area topologically valid.

notes: VERIFIED — read Reshaping Polygons and Chained Elements; companion pages Adding Element Nodes and Curve/Straighten Element Edge cover insert-node and curve-edge; chained elements are treated as a temporary polygon.

statement: Convert selected elements that have a 3D representation, including library objects and their sub-components, into independent Morphs.
superiority: Lossless conversion reports property and relationship loss.

acceptance.sketch: Slab to Morph preserves volume to 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Create Morph from Existing Elements; only Convert Selection to Morph(s) was found; wall-to-slab or fill-to-slab conversions are not documented, so the row is narrowed to Morph conversion.

statement: Explode selected construction elements, library objects, dimensions and polylines in a 2D window into basic drawing primitives such as lines, arcs, fills and text, optionally keeping the originals.
superiority: Explosion keeps material and layer mapping.

acceptance.sketch: Explode object into 3D: Morph volume equals bounding sum.

notes: CORRECTED — read Explode into Current View; output is 2D only (3D-to-Morph conversion is the separate command in EDIT-0019); grouped and locked elements are skipped.

statement: Move a wall's reference line relative to its geometry, flip it in place, and mirror its doors and windows through one dialog, without displacing the wall in plan.
superiority: Reference line editing accessible via Python as well.

acceptance.sketch: Pet palette on wall: offset reference line and observe change.

notes: CORRECTED — read Modify Wall Reference Line; the dialog offers Mirror Walls in Place, Mirror Doors and Windows, reference line location and offset; no effect on complex profile walls; slab reference plane is a separate topic.

statement: Select or deselect elements by combined criteria such as element type, layer, parameters, properties and classifications, using built-in or user-stored criteria sets and an optional marquee restriction.
superiority: Saved queries reusable in schedules and scripts.

acceptance.sketch: Query returns only elements satisfying AND of criteria; count matches.

notes: VERIFIED — read Find and Select Elements (palette, Plus/Minus buttons, pick-up of settings from an element) and Predefined Criteria Sets (store, rename, export as XML).

statement: Select every element in the window, or every element of the active tool's type, on the current story with one command, and use context commands that jump the selection between the floor plan and 3D.
superiority: Includes selection by property expression.

acceptance.sketch: Select all walls count equals count.

notes: CORRECTED — read Special Selection Commands; Select All (single type) is Ctrl+A with a tool active; a 'Select Similar' command was not found in the help.

statement: Draw a polygonal, rectangular or rotated-rectangle selection area with partial, entire or direction-dependent inclusion logic, and use Shift to add to or remove from the selection.
superiority: Selection previews counts by type.

acceptance.sketch: Crossing marquee selects partially inside elements.

notes: CORRECTED — read Draw Selection Area and Deselect Elements; no line-marquee mode exists; direction rule: right-to-left selects whole elements, left-to-right selects partial ones.

statement: Show only the selected elements in a 3D window, or hide the current selection there, from the context menu.
superiority: Isolation applies to layouts and exports as view states.

acceptance.sketch: Isolation hides other elements and restores on exit.

notes: CORRECTED — read Special Selection Commands; Show Selection in 3D and Hide Selection in 3D exist; isolating in a section window was not found.

statement: Show temporary snap guides along existing elements and user-marked snap references, let input lock to a guide with a key, and offer snap points at chosen divisions along edges.
superiority: Snap results can be queried and logged by tests.

acceptance.sketch: Cursor near midpoint snaps to exact midpoint within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Snap Guides and Snap Points; guides include horizontal/vertical, parallel to grid and fixed-angle; tangent snapping is not documented and Gravity is a separate placement aid.

statement: Type exact coordinates, distances and angles into an on-screen Tracker using direct entry, Tab or axis shortcuts, including arithmetic expressions, with Shift-based input constraints on direction.
superiority: Command-line style input available for all tools.

acceptance.sketch: Typed dx 3 dy 2 produces exact vector.

notes: CORRECTED — read Tracker and Input Constraints and Guides dialog; field shortcuts X/Y/Z/D/A, math expressions like 20+ and 3*, Shift constrains to horizontal/vertical or an incremental angle.

statement: Snap the cursor to nodes of a construction grid or a separate snap grid, and place permanent guide lines and guide circles by dragging from window-edge tabs or drawing a segment.
superiority: Guide lines serialised and shared across views.

acceptance.sketch: Guide line at x=5 snaps exact.

notes: CORRECTED — read Guide Lines and Snap to Grid; guide lines come from window-edge tabs, the Ruler or a two-click segment (not simply from rulers); grid snap toggles with Alt+S.

statement: Undo and redo a configurable number of construction steps, with the next step's command name shown in the menu and the queue cleared by events such as changing story heights.
superiority: Branching undo history with named checkpoints.

acceptance.sketch: 50 edits undo to original state byte-equal in model hash.

notes: CORRECTED — read Basic Editing Operations; limit is the Undo Limit in Data Safety & Integrity; navigator operations are not undoable; no browsable history list is documented.

statement: Cut, copy and paste elements within and across projects, re-pasting at the original position between stories, matching attributes by name, with a dialog for locked or hidden layers.
superiority: Cross-project paste keeps attributes by name mapping and flags conflicts.

acceptance.sketch: Paste in place keeps coordinates; paste to other story shifts by story offset.

notes: CORRECTED — read Basic Editing Operations; same-position paste between stories and a Paste Options dialog exist; a command named Paste Aligned was not found; paste into section windows yields 2D primitives only.

statement: Copy, cut or delete all elements of chosen types from one story to another through a single Edit Elements by Stories dialog.

source.ref: Edit Elements by Stories Dialog Box

superiority: Visual feedback and dry-run report.

acceptance.sketch: Home story becomes target story.

notes: CORRECTED — read Edit Elements by Stories Dialog Box; cross-story copy is dialog-based; per-story windows to drag between were not found (Drag & Drop page covers transfer to other applications).

statement: Open the tool settings dialog for the current selection, showing selected and editable counts, and apply a changed setting to all editable selected elements.

source.ref: Working in Tool Settings Dialog Boxes

superiority: Mixed-value fields show diff and allow partial apply.

acceptance.sketch: Changing layer on 5 mixed elements applies to all.

notes: CORRECTED — read Working in Tool Settings Dialog Boxes; title bar distinguishes Default vs Selected settings; explicit mixed-value display was not found on this page.

statement: Pick up the parameters of one element and inject them into other elements of the same type, using named transfer sets that choose which settings are copied.
superiority: Transfer can target a saved query.

acceptance.sketch: Inject only fill pen: other fields unchanged.

notes: VERIFIED — read Parameter Transfer and Element Transfer Settings; Alt picks up, Ctrl+Alt injects, last-used transfer set shown and switchable; Morph face/edge variants exist.

statement: Assign element IDs in bulk by element type, sort criteria and a formatted counter pattern, on the selection or on all visible elements.
superiority: Spatial and rule-based renumbering with collision detection.

acceptance.sketch: Pattern W-### renumbers 1..N in spatial order.

notes: CORRECTED — read Element ID Manager; text, counter and story-number components, with saved settings; a dedicated zone renumber command was not found.

statement: Edit a selected wall through context pet palette commands such as stretching an end, trapezoid stretch, curving an edge and angular or radial stretch of curved walls.
superiority: Pet palette items accessible as commands and API.

acceptance.sketch: Pet palette curvature on straight wall converts to arc preserving ends.

notes: CORRECTED — read Stretching Walls, Curve/Straighten Element Edge and Pet Palettes; offset and slant commands were not confirmed on these pages; pet palette contents vary by element and are not customisable.

statement: Edit slab and roof polygons through pet palette commands such as offset edge, insert node, add or subtract polygon, and, for roofs, change pitch or levels.
superiority: Applies identical logic to surfaces of any element.

acceptance.sketch: Offset edge of slab by 0.2 changes area per formula.

notes: CORRECTED — read Graphical Editing of Roof Geometry and Modify the Roof Pitch; roof pivot line, ridge, levels and contour are editable; applying a change to several edges at once was not confirmed.

statement: Add a newly drawn polygon to, or subtract it from, a selected polygonal element through pet palette commands, also doable with the Magic Wand.
superiority: Polygonal operations stay exact on arc segments.

acceptance.sketch: Subtracting an inner polygon from a slab creates a hole of exactly that area.

notes: CORRECTED — read Reshaping Polygons and Chained Elements; only Add to Polygon and Subtract from Polygon are described; an intersect operation is not documented.

statement: Show a live preview of the element in its settings dialog that updates as the parameters change.

source.ref: Beam Tool Settings: Preview and Positioning

superiority: Previews rendered from the same engine as views.

acceptance.sketch: Dialog preview shows updated composite.

notes: CORRECTED — read Beam Tool Settings: Preview and Positioning; the preview stays visible on every page and reflects changes; separate 2D and 3D preview modes were not confirmed.

statement: Clean up colliding wall junctions automatically by building-material skin priority, where wall-to-wall joins also require the reference lines to intersect.
superiority: Cleanup logic open and deterministic.

acceptance.sketch: Cleaned T junction shows no visible line in the core.

notes: CORRECTED — read Specific Element Intersections and Junctions, Basic Intersection Principles; a 'Marquee Cut Plane Wall Cleanup' command was not found; layer intersection groups can prevent connections.

statement: Control which of several equal-priority walls or beams meets first at a junction through a numeric Junction Order set in the element settings.
superiority: Junction mode is shown graphically on the model.

acceptance.sketch: On a T junction, changing priority moves the skin cut line to the expected position.

notes: CORRECTED — read Specific Element Intersections and Junctions and Beam Tool Settings; Junction Order (higher wins) is the documented fix for equal priorities; no separate wall-junction reshape command found.

statement: Nudge selected elements with the arrow keys by the snap-grid increment, and by the construction-grid spacing when Shift is held.
superiority: Show the nudge step on screen and let it follow the current zoom or a typed value, merged into one undo step per burst.

acceptance.sketch: Set snap increment to 50 mm; press Right three times: selection moves exactly +150 mm in x; Shift+Right moves by construction grid spacing.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Nudging Elements; step comes from Snap Grid/Nudge in Grids & Background; Shift uses Construction Grid spacing; works in 3D along the horizontal plane.

statement: Adjust selected walls, columns or horizontal beams to the top or bottom (or core top and core bottom) of the slab above, below or both, keeping door and window offsets.
superiority: Preview the resulting heights and offer a project-wide fix-up of every wall-to-slab gap in one undoable step.

acceptance.sketch: Wall bottom at slab finish top, adjust to Core Top: wall base drops to core top exactly; a bottom-linked door keeps its absolute position.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Adjust Elements to Slabs; chooses the nearest slab unless slabs are selected; recalculates the offset of a door/window linked to a wall bottom.

statement: Special Align lines selected elements up by a chosen anchor point (such as the nearest point of each bounding box) onto a drawn or existing line, arc or edge.
superiority: Show anchor choice and result live on the canvas and keep the alignment as an optional constraint rather than a one-off move.

acceptance.sketch: Three objects aligned by nearest point to a line y=10: each element's bounding-box point closest to the line lies exactly on y=10 afterwards.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Align Elements; Special Align options pick which point aligns and the target (temporary line/arc or existing edge); plain Align uses bounding boxes.

statement: Use a Magic Wand to trace a linear or polygonal shape from existing elements, or the closed area around a clicked point, and create a new element of the active tool's type from it.
superiority: Trace across mixed 2D and 3D geometry with live preview of every candidate region and a one-key cycle between them.

acceptance.sketch: With four lines forming a closed square, wand-click inside with the Fill tool: a fill with exactly the square's boundary is created.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Magic Wand; Spacebar activates it; clicking an edge traces a chain, clicking empty space traces the bounded area; preselecting elements limits what is considered.

statement: Choose the Magic Wand tracing method (best-match curves or linear segments only) and the curve approximation by deviation, segments per arc or circle, or segment length.
superiority: Make the curve approximation visible as a live overlay and remember it per element type.

acceptance.sketch: Trace a circle of radius 1 with maximum deviation 0.01: every polygon vertex lies on the circle and every chord sagitta is at most 0.01.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Magic Wand Settings; options are Deviation from Curves, Segments Along Arcs, Segments Along Circles and Segment Length.

statement: Show temporary snap points on hovered edges at halves, a set number of divisions, a percentage or a fixed distance measured from an endpoint or midpoint.
superiority: Allow user-defined division rules saved per project and combined with snap guides.

acceptance.sketch: Edge of length 10 with Divisions=4: snap points appear at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 from the start; with Distance=3 from endpoint: 3, 6 and 9.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Snap Points; intervals are Half, Divisions (3-100), Percent, Distance and Best Division by Distance; points auto-hide after about five seconds unless disabled.

statement: Gravity places newly created walls, columns, beams and objects at the elevation of the slab, roof, shell or mesh under the cursor.
superiority: Apply gravity to moved elements too, not only new ones, and show the supporting surface live.

acceptance.sketch: Place a column at (x,y) over a slab whose top is z=3.0 with gravity on: column base elevation is 3.0; with no surface below it uses the tool's default elevation.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Gravity; used only when placing new elements; level dimensions placed with gravity associate to the surface; 3D uses Surface Snap instead.

statement: Draw overlapping elements in a class-based stacking order and let the user bring forward, send backward, bring to front, send to back or reset an element's position in it.
superiority: Expose a single layer-like draw-order list per view with drag reordering and per-view overrides.

acceptance.sketch: Place a fill over an object in default order then Bring to Front on the fill: fill draws above the object; Reset Default Order restores the object on top.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Display Order; six element classes, 14 stack levels, annotation always above 2D artwork by default; commands in Edit > Display Order.

statement: Store a selection from any window as a named selection set in a palette, and later redefine it, replace the current selection with it, add it to it or subtract it.

source.ref: Store Selection Sets in Selections Palette

superiority: Keep selection sets live across windows and share them with the team, not only per project window.

acceptance.sketch: Save a selection of 5 walls, deselect, click X on the set: exactly those 5 walls are selected again; click minus: they are deselected.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Store Selection Sets in Selections Palette; stored with the project; list sortable by name or window of origin.

statement: Define named element transfer sets that choose which settings are copied during parameter injection and when applying favorites, with one default for favorites, and export or import them.
superiority: Show a diff of what a transfer set would change before injecting and offer per-project sharing as plain JSON.

acceptance.sketch: Set that excludes pen settings: inject from a pen-5 wall to a pen-2 wall: pen stays 2 and all other included parameters change.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Element Transfer Settings; sets are stored with the project, the favorites default is a local user preference, import/export is XML.

statement: Define a marquee area on the current story or on all stories (polygonal, rectangle or rotated rectangle) and use it to select, move, resize, copy or view only that part of the model.
superiority: Allow the marquee to be saved as a named region and reused for views, selections and exports.

acceptance.sketch: Rectangle marquee over 3 of 10 walls, Select All in Marquee: exactly the 3 walls inside (partial inclusion rule) are selected.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Marquee Area and Marquee Area Definition; Single Story vs All Stories methods, 3D marquee defines base then height; Ctrl+A selects all inside.
